name: Payments & Fintech
one_liner: Payments and fintech firms move money and extend financial services through software, earning small fees on very large volumes where scale and network effects dominate.
how_it_makes_money: Most payments revenue is a take rate on transaction volume, split among card networks, issuers (interchange), acquirers and processors. Fintechs also earn from lending spreads, subscriptions, interest on customer balances, and software fees.
revenue_formula: Payments revenue = total payment volume (TPV) × take rate
TPV = active users or merchants × transactions per user × average ticket
Fintech lending revenue = loan balances × (yield - funding cost - credit losses)
cost_structure: Transaction costs: interchange and network fees passed through to issuers and networks
Customer acquisition: marketing, incentives and sales teams
Technology and engineering: platform, reliability, security
Fraud and credit losses: chargebacks and loan defaults
Compliance and risk: licensing, AML/KYC, bank partnerships
margins: Card networks run very high operating margins (often ~50%+) thanks to asset-light scale, while processors, acquirers and many fintechs earn thin margins on net revenue; the spread is driven by scale, pricing power, and loss rates.

key_metrics.name: Total payment volume (TPV)
key_metrics.what: Dollar value of transactions processed; the core scale measure.

key_metrics.name: Take rate
key_metrics.what: Net revenue as a share of TPV; shows pricing power and value added per transaction.

key_metrics.name: Transaction margin
key_metrics.what: Revenue minus transaction and loss costs; the true unit economics after pass-throughs.

key_metrics.name: Customer acquisition cost (CAC) / LTV
key_metrics.what: Cost to win a user versus the lifetime profit they generate; tests growth efficiency.

key_metrics.name: Active users / merchants
key_metrics.what: Accounts transacting in a period; drives network effects and cross-sell.

key_metrics.name: Fraud and loss rate
key_metrics.what: Losses as a share of volume; small changes swing profitability.

trends: Real-time payments rails (FedNow, RTP) and account-to-account payments challenging cards
Embedded finance letting software platforms offer payments, lending and cards
Consolidation and profitability focus after the fintech funding boom
Buy now, pay later expanding and drawing regulatory attention
Scrutiny of bank-fintech partnerships and ongoing interchange debates
Stablecoins and tokenized money gaining traction in payments
